# Protocol increment hard-requires a field the released counterpart never sends (P0)

Pattern: a client-side increment of a two-sided protocol change (e.g., enhanced-settings "application receipt") made a new response field mandatory (`response.get("applied") is not True` → raise), unconditionally (not gated on the feature flag or a capability signal). The released/supported provider (git tag `eval-release`, `provider/settings.py`) returns only `{"ok": True}` and has already persisted the values, so every ordinary save fails after the write was applied → breaks independent releasability and causes misreported failures / duplicate retries.

Companion smell: the unit-test fake was updated to return the NEW protocol shape (`{"ok": True, "applied": True}`), so the suite passes while the supported-provider shape is untested.

Check in future reviews: when one side of a split client/provider change lands first, verify the new code against the supported counterpart's actual response (README names the baseline tag), keep a compatibility test using the baseline response shape, and gate strict checks behind a flag/capability until the counterpart is the supported baseline.
